You are a senior UI/UX designer and professional healthcare website content writer.

Task:
Create a high-quality, modern, and trustworthy website for a Diagnostic / Pathology Lab.

Website Goals:
• Build strong trust for new patients
• Clearly showcase blood tests and full body checkup packages
• Increase WhatsApp bookings
• Present offers and promotions professionally
• Make location, services, and credibility very clear

Target Audience:
Local patients and families looking for reliable blood tests and health checkups.

Design Requirements:
• Clean, medical, premium look (white + light blue / green theme)
• Modern card-based layout
• Mobile-first, fast loading
• Professional icons and sections
• No clutter, high readability
• CTA buttons: “Book on WhatsApp”, “Call Now”

Pages Required:
1. Home
2. Tests & Packages
3. Offers
4. About Us
5. Contact / Location

For EACH PAGE provide:
• Section-wise layout (hero, cards, CTA, etc.)
• Exact headline text
• Supporting content text
• CTA button text
• UI/UX notes (spacing, layout, visual hierarchy)

Home Page Must Include:
• Strong trust headline
• Key services overview
• Popular test packages
• Why choose us (trust points)
• WhatsApp booking CTA
• Location & contact preview

Tests & Packages Page:
• Categories: Blood Tests, Full Body Checkups, Preventive Packages
• Pricing card layout
• Clear benefits of each package

Offers Page:
• Limited-time offers
• Discount badge ideas
• Urgency-based CTA copy

About Us Page:
• Trust-focused lab introduction
• Experience, accuracy, hygiene, reports timing
• Patient-first approach

Contact Page:
• Address
• Google Maps embed placeholder
• WhatsApp & Call CTA
• Working hours

Extra:
• Write content in simple professional English
• Avoid technical jargon
• Sound reliable, medical, and premium
• Do NOT write code
• Output should be ready-to-use website content & layout guide

**Initiating Website Design**

I'm focusing now on understanding the user's ultimate goal: a trustworthy, modern website for a Diagnostic/Pathology Lab. This initial phase involves a deep dive into required quality, and building trust, as well as the expected features of the site. I am beginning to identify key components.


**Defining Technical Specifications**

I've determined the technical stack for the project: React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS will form the foundation. I also have confirmed goals around building trust, showcasing service packages, prompting WhatsApp bookings, and highlighting offers. The tech will focus on a single XML block output.


**Outlining Core Components**

I'm now focusing on the application's structure. I'm visualizing the `App.tsx` layout and routing, and I've detailed components such as the Header, Footer, Hero, PackageCard, FeatureSection, and a reusable Button. Additionally, I've outlined the core pages: Home, Packages, Offers, About, and Contact.

**Content and Brand Identity**

I've sketched out the core content and branding elements. I've settled on "PrimeDiag Labs" as the lab name. The color palette will be Sky Blue, Teal/Emerald, White, and Gray. The navigation structure is now finalized. I've also prepared the WhatsApp link for integration.

**Sequencing Implementation Steps**

My implementation plan now includes sequential steps for development. First, I'll start by defining the application's metadata within a `metadata.json` file. Second, I will focus on implementing the `index.html` file.


**Detailing Implementation Steps**

I've outlined specific HTML structure and Tailwind CDN integration. Subsequently, the React root rendering in `index.tsx`, along with the `App.tsx`'s `HashRouter`, Navbar, Routes, and Footer, are also being created. Shared components, including the `Button` with various variants, a consistent `Section` wrapper, and the base-styled `Card`, are now being designed. The basic structure of the pages is also taking shape. I am designing a home page with an image and featured packages.

**Finalizing Visuals**

I am now putting in the final touches for the user interface. I'm focusing on Tailwind's specific implementation of shadows and rounded corners. I've decided to use `shadow-lg` on the cards, along with `rounded-2xl`, for a friendly look and feel. I am designing the hero section to have a subtle gradient.


**Implementing Technical Elements**

My current focus is on the specific technical elements. I've decided on the "medical" seed for the hero image and am sourcing icons from `lucide-react`, specifically `Phone`, `Menu`, `X`, `MapPin`, `Clock`, `ShieldCheck`, `Microscope`, `TestTube`, and `Percentage`. Package data will be managed in a reusable `constants.ts` file. I'm also confirming the design constraints, ensuring adherence to no external CSS files, React 18, TypeScript, and the single XML output requirement. I have also designed for future Gemini API inclusion.


**Refining Content and Structure**

I'm now integrating the user's specific content directly into the React components. I've defined `Package`, `Test`, and `Offer` types in `types.ts`, and populated `constants.ts` with mock data. I am creating `components/Layout.tsx` for header/footer wrapping, and starting on `pages/Home.tsx` as the main landing, and `pages/Packages.tsx` for the detailed list. I also have fixed the WhatsApp link to open in a new tab. I plan a final polish, ensuring prominence for the "Book on WhatsApp" button, and maintaining the trustworthy blue/green palette. Lastly, I will generate the XML.


**Generating XML Output**

I'm now in the final stretch, and focusing on the XML generation. I've been working on a function that transforms all relevant data into a clean XML structure. It includes packages, offers, and all the content elements. My aim is a valid, single XML block that meets all requirements, ready for the user to implement. I have confirmed that this completes the project.
